_about.what: Built-in data for an offline 'plan, place devices, BOM' program spun out of the Quartzite Design tab.
_about.generated: 2026-11-19, by running the repository's own modules (bundled with esbuild) and dumping their exported constants; prose strings were written by hand from the same files.
_about.units: Feet unless a key says otherwise. Template polygons: x right, y DOWN, origin at the top-left of the drawing's bounding box, stage/platform at the top.
_about.noDollars: The app carries no built-in equipment prices: every equation item is priced from an Equipment map that starts empty. Only the seed fabric rates and the percentage defaults below are money-related.

tiers.note: referenceCostMul / referencePriceMul are inert for map-priced systems (every system priced from the Equipment map is 'tierFixed' and ignores them). A tier changes price only through (a) which part is mapped per tier, (b) the line-set dial, (c) the tier multipliers on Cable Package, wire pull and labor.

lineSetDial.meaning: null = the equation's own line-set count (rigSets); a number 1-300 rescales every rigging quantity by dial / rigSets, each rounded, never below 0.

gridScopes.note: Every placed device has exactly one scope, computed from its part (part.gridScope, else catalog group, else trade, else Unscoped). Curtains print with Rigging on the R sheets.

sizePresets.rule: Picking a venue or a size sets each of width/depth/grid/wing/ph to clamp(round(base x multiplier), min, max). The size key (small/medium/large) ALSO drives the equations' pick(small, medium, large) factors independently of the typed dimensions.

venueKinds.clampRule: A non-number becomes the range midpoint; anything else is clamped to [min, max]. Applied on every save and every geometry read.
venueKinds.houseFieldRules: House-field limits and defaults depend on the other fields - see venueTemplates.<id>.houseFields. A blank house field means 'use the default'.
venueKinds.hiddenDimsNote: A venue kind that does not show a field still carries its value (used by the equations): e.g. a church has ph 18 and wing 0.

venueTypes.note: CRM venue types (Settings > Venue types). Each 'works like' a built-in kind and has a Background template. A design draws: its own template override, else its venue type's Background, else the kind default.

venueTemplates._note: Simplified outlines at each template's own drawn size: inside faces of the named areas, curves sampled to short straight runs (arena outlines thinned to about 30 points). Enough to draw a base plan and to place by rule; not the full drawing (the full line work is src/lib/design/venue-templates/<kind>.json, 12-75 segments each, drawing inches, y up).

canvas.note: The app lays a stretched template on a 640 px wide canvas and stores placements as fractions 0..1 of that sheet. An offline program can use feet directly.

proscenium@1.label: Auditorium / PAC
proscenium@1.drawnAtNote: The size the source drawing was made at (the stretch is the identity here). proWidthFt/wingFt/stageDepthFt/houseWidthFt/houseDepthFt are the engine's generic stretch inputs; see stretch.inputs for what each means in this template.

inputs.houseWidthFt: House width (inside walls at the back)
inputs.houseDepthFt: House depth (plaster line to back wall)

stretch.sideToSide: Symmetric about the centreline. From the stage down to the stage edge's lowest point: the opening's half follows proscenium width / 2, then each wing follows wing width; outer walls keep 6 in. At the back of the house: the booth and vestibules (the middle 35 ft 4.5 in) keep their size and the rest follows house width. Between those two lines the mapping blends linearly, so the house side walls splay (or slant inward when the house is narrower than the stage).
stretch.frontToBack: The plaster line never moves. Above it the stage follows stage depth; the back wall stays 6 in. Below it the proscenium wall, forestage, pit and stage-edge curve keep their size (about 15 ft); the catwalk band (4 ft 8 in) and the cross aisle / curved back wall / booth row (about 27 ft 4 in) keep their size; the two seating spans between them share whatever is left of house depth in proportion to their drawn lengths (4.28 ft and 28.5 ft).
stretch.other: The Pit region, its lines and its label are hidden when the pit system is off. The stage-edge curve and the curved house back wall are sampled arcs that follow the map.

houseFields.warning: House narrower than proscenium width + 2 x wing: 'The house is narrower than the stage, so its side walls slant inward.'

church-traditional@1.label: Church — Traditional
church-traditional@1.drawnAtNote: The size the source drawing was made at (the stretch is the identity here). proWidthFt/wingFt/stageDepthFt/houseWidthFt/houseDepthFt are the engine's generic stretch inputs; see stretch.inputs for what each means in this template.

inputs.stageDepthFt: Platform depth (front edge to back wall)
inputs.houseDepthFt: Nave depth (platform front to the back-room wall)

stretch.sideToSide: Above the back-room wall: the chancel follows platform width; the chancel wall, the front step's overhang and the notch wall keep their size (about 4 ft 9 in each side); the side rooms (Choir Room left, Electrical Room right) absorb the rest out to the nave's inside face. At and below the back-room wall: the Entry and its walls (about 20 ft 2.5 in wide) keep their size; Cry Room and Storage absorb the rest.
stretch.frontToBack: The platform front never moves. The chancel's back part follows platform depth; the notch wall, side-room wall and the 7 ft front step keep their size (7 ft 6 in); the nave follows nave depth; the back rooms and outer wall keep their size (about 12 ft 8 in).
stretch.other: The apse stays a true arc: radius and chord scale with platform width. No booth room - the FOH mix position (62 % of the nave's depth, on the centreline) stands in for it. Pews are drawn by code: straight rows every 3 ft from 6 ft behind the platform front to 8 ft short of the back wall, 4 ft clear of the nave walls, split by a 5 ft centre aisle lined up with the Entry.

houseFields.warning: Typed width below the minimum: 'The nave needs 8' beside the platform on each side, so the plan widens it to fit.'

For the arena these are court width, bowl depth, court length and the floor's straight runs (floor 90 x 134 ft); the end stage is shown at 40 x 16 ft.

stretch.sideToSide: From the centre out: the court's half (court width = floor width x 300/540), the floor's straight run, the 13 ft corner radius (fixed), then the bowl (bowl depth).
stretch.frontToBack: Same, mirrored about the centre: court length = floor length x 564/804, straight run, 13 ft corner radius, bowl.
stretch.other: Floor and bowl are true rounded rectangles (floor corner radius 13 ft; bowl corner radius 13 ft + bowl depth, same centres, so the bowl is an even band). Single lines, no wall thickness. Booth and Electrical Room (10 ft x 44 ft 8 in) move along the bowl's four straight outer sides (home: left and right). The end stage is a code-drawn rectangle (stage width x stage depth) that moves along the floor's four straight edges (home: top end, centred); it is shrunk to fit - no longer than that edge's straight run (edge length minus 26 ft) and no deeper than half the floor across it - with the warning 'The stage is bigger than the floor takes there, so the plan shrinks it to fit.'

curtainGeometry.note: Each curtain line also carries the finished geometry its cost is computed from. PW = W, PH = proscenium height. Geometry does not change with tier.
curtainGeometry.costPerDrape: round( finishedWidth x (1 + fullness/100) x finishedHeight x fabric $/sq ft x (1 + sewing%/100) x max(1, panels) ) - a cost; sell = cost x (1 + catalog markup)
curtainGeometry.fabricRateChain: part.curtainAreaRate, else the seed rate for that SKU, else part.costPerSqft, else part.cost when the part's unit is sq ft, else 0 (the line needs a part)
curtainGeometry.gridCurtainFromAuto: Auto fill drops ONE Grid curtain per unit: width = panel width x panels (rounded to 0.1 ft), height = finished height, fullness as above, type Draw/Leg/Border/Full.

pipeline: 1. compute(state) -> item keys and quantities per system (no dollars).
2. Line-set dial: when the tier's dial differs from rigSets, every rigging quantity = max(0, round(qty x dial / rigSets)).
3. Cable Package: re-derived for the tier being priced from the EFFECTIVE fixture quantities (a typed quantity override wins).
4. Wire pull: one 'Wire pull' line per wire system (rigging, lighting, controls, audio, video) that is on and whose runs > 0.
5. Price every line from the Equipment map cell for that tier (or a per-design swap). Unmapped -> $0, status 'needs a part'.
6. Quick Design only: the tier's typed quantity overrides replace quantities (whole numbers >= 0).

cablePackage.formula: qty = ceil( round(fixtures x perFixture x tierMult x 1000) / 1000 )
cablePackage.note: '24 fixtures x 1 x 1.15' is shown beside the line.

wirePull.formula: feet = ceil( round((stageWidth + stageDepth + houseDepth) x runs x tierMult x 1000) / 1000 )
wirePull.houseDepth: always missing (no form asks for it) -> counts 0 and the line carries the note 'House depth isn't in the design - not counted'

labor.formula: per system: labor = priced material (sell) x labor% / 100 x tierMult
labor.laborPctFallback: an unset system % takes the stored legacy flat install % ('system.installPct'), else 18

quickDesignTotals.material: sum over systems that are on of (qty x unit sell)
quickDesignTotals.install: round(sum over systems of material x labor fraction)
quickDesignTotals.contingency: round(subtotal x contingency% / 100); default 10, whole number 0-25
quickDesignTotals.grand: subtotal + contingency, shown in whole dollars

pricing.part: sell = the part's list price, else cost x (1 + catalog markup); cost = the part's cost. A part with neither -> needs a part.
pricing.assembly: cost and sell from the assembly's included members; sell falls back to cost x (1 + markup)
pricing.allowance: unit cost = the confirmed amount; sell = cost x (1 + markup)
pricing.catalogMarkupDefault: the catalog's default markup setting; the code's default is 0.43 (43 %). An unusable value (negative or >= 19) falls back to 0.43.
pricing.incompleteRule: If any line with quantity > 0 on a system that is on prices 'needs a part', the estimate shows 'Incomplete - N items need a part' instead of a dollar total and cannot be promoted to a quote.

deviceTypes.note: The 25 seeded device types. key = slug of the label. code = the designator prefix. icon = glyph id in the app's Grid icon set. An admin can add types (max 60), archive them, change code / icon / drawing, and map catalog categories to types.
deviceTypes.codeRule: 1-6 characters A-Z / 0-9, upper-cased, unique among active types. A type with no code: the shipped default above, else the first letters of up to three words of its label, or the first three letters of a one-word label; 'DEV' if empty.

legacyShapes.note: The older per-category shape setting; markers now draw the device type's icon inside a scope-coloured tile, falling back to these shapes.

wireTypes.note: Default wire types (Grid Settings > Wire types; max 60). A wire type carries one or more connection types; two ports connect when one wire type carries both ports' connection types and directions are compatible. speaker-pair is the only 'interchangeable' family. symbol / signal / cableSku are blank until 'Add starter cables' or 'Fill symbols from Bray's legend' fills them.

titleBlockFields: company name, address lines, phone, logo (the office marked as the quote default, else the first)
project id (GRD-####), project name, customer, venue, address

designators.numbering: Per code within one design option. New devices take the lowest free number (a lot of N needs N consecutive free numbers). Gaps are kept until Renumber.
designators.lot: A lot marker of quantity N stores its first number and shows a range: LX-1–24.

padding.setting: digits 1 or 2 (app setting; 2 is the default since the conduit riser shipped)
padding.rule: at 2 digits numbers below 10 print with a leading zero (CRO-01); 123 prints 123

codeResolution: the part's own designator code, when it has one
else the part's device type's code
else (part not mapped to a type) the placement's category, then the part's category, through the category->type map
else the system letter of the part's scope: L, A, V, R (Rigging and Curtains) or G
designators.readingOrder: sheet order, page, space (project order; devices in no space last), rows of 0.02 of the sheet height top to bottom, then left to right; id breaks ties
designators.custom: Anything that is not <code>-<number> is a custom designator: shown as typed, never renumbered, never counted. Max 24 characters; control and invisible characters stripped; 'MIC - 1' becomes 'MIC-1'; a typed range keeps its first number.
designators.duplicates: Overlapping number blocks in the same code (case-insensitive), or equal custom text, are drawn amber (#b7791f). Not blocked.
designators.replacePart: A number issued in the old type's code is re-issued in the new code when the code changes; a custom or hand-renamed designator is kept.

renumber.rule: Re-issue from the lowest numbers not held by untargeted devices of that code, in reading order. 'Apply current type codes' re-issues each device in its current type code.

placementRules.coordinates: x, y as fractions 0..1 of the sheet page

autoFill.note: See design-spec.md chapter 5 for the placement formulas.
